summary.intent: Execute Phase 60 (IPNS Verification Cross-Layer Closeout) using wave-based sequential subagent execution across 8 plans in 4 waves, hardening IPNS verification to be strictly fail-closed across Rust and TypeScript layers.
summary.outcome: Waves 1 and 2 partially completed: 60-01 through 60-04 finished (4/8 plans), with Wave 2 still in progress at plan 60-05 when the transcript ends. All completed plans passed build/test gates.

repo: Phase 60 has 8 plans across 4 waves: Wave 1 (60-01, 60-02, 60-03), Wave 2 (60-04, 60-05, 60-07), Wave 3 (60-06), Wave 4 (60-08 — non-autonomous operational cutover requiring human action).

60-01 moved the verified-IPNS-resolve chokepoint from crates/fuse/src/verify.rs into crates/api-client/src/ipns.rs and removed VerifyError::Legacy, folding all 9 FUSE caller arms as a compile necessity (pre-empting 60-04's declared scope).
60-02 unified all 9 first-publish IPNS producers to embed sequence=1 instead of sequence=0 (D-02), a precondition for the strict resolve verifier.
60-03 hardened the TypeScript resolveIpnsRecord to fail-closed: deleted legacy else fall-through, dropped first-publish skew disjunct, added CBOR Validity EOL/expiry enforcement (D-07 TS path).
60-04 deleted crates/fuse/src/verify.rs entirely after routing remaining Rust resolve paths fail-closed; no lingering references remained.
sdk-core has 251 tests including 34 ipns-specific tests; all passed after Wave 1.
cipherbox-api-client gained ciborium + cipherbox-core dependencies via 60-01's CBOR Validity parsing (Cargo.toml edited but Cargo.lock not committed by executor — a latent --locked CI break).

Plan 60-05 scope: require seq=1 on first publish (D-03), make parseCachedRecord return null/404 when DB signed_record is NULL, remove implicit DB-sequence override and nullable-pubKey/cached-signature legacy enrich branches on resolve (D-06).
Plan 60-06 (Wave 3): API publish-path verify cache for CPU cost recovery.
Plan 60-08 (Wave 4): staging wipe + redeploy + smoke-test — non-autonomous, requires human action.

Deleted by 60-04 after all re-exports and consumer imports were re-pointed to api-client.

workflow: Sequential gsd-executor subagents on the main working tree were chosen over worktree-isolated agents because there is no reliable mechanism to merge back worktree branches after parallel execution in this harness.
The gsd commit helper reports 'commit_failed' / 'No staged files match any configured task' even when the commit actually lands — a known false-negative that must be verified with git log.

Executors may fold cross-plan scope as a compile necessity (60-01 folded all 9 FUSE Legacy arms that were declared in 60-04's scope) — this is acceptable but should be noted in STATE/ROADMAP to avoid duplicate work.
Mid-edit diagnostic snapshots from executors can be stale — always verify compilation directly with cargo check rather than trusting executor-reported errors at face value.
Cargo.lock changes from Cargo.toml edits must be explicitly tracked and committed; sequential executor subagents do not reliably catch and commit lockfile drift, creating latent --locked CI failures.
Post-wave build gates (cargo check + full test suite) are essential for catching cross-plan integration issues before advancing to the next wave.

friction: gsd commit helper returned a false-negative 'commit_failed' / 'No staged files match any configured task' even though the Cargo.lock commit landed successfully — required a follow-up git log to confirm.
60-01's executor left Cargo.lock uncommitted after editing Cargo.toml, creating a latent --locked CI break that was only caught by manual inspection after 60-04.
60-01's executor appended a stray self-check footer to 60-01-SUMMARY.md after its SUMMARY commit, resulting in a factually incorrect artifact that required manual revert.

Mid-execution diagnostic from 60-01 executor incorrectly reported a compile error (metadata.rs:619 VerifyError::Legacy) that was actually already resolved — required manual cargo check to confirm the tree was green.
Worktree isolation mode (Agent tool's isolation='worktree') is incompatible with this harness's merge-back requirements, forcing sequential execution and sacrificing parallelism.
